claim: v0.9 formalizes a Plugin Stability Lifecycle (Alpha, Beta, Stable) for every router plugin; Alpha plugins require the --allow-experimental-plugins flag to activate, and automated dependency validation checks a plugin's prerequisites before the router starts.
stance_target: governance/maturity gating a custom backend-discovery plugin must pass through before production use
scope_conditions: llm-d v0.9 release (v0.10 milestone targets September 2026, implying v0.9 is mid-to-late 2026)
quoted_support: Plugin stability lifecycle formalizes the maturity of every router plugin as Alpha, Beta, or Stable. Alpha plugins require `--allow-experimental-plugins` to activate, preventing accidental use of unproven extensions in production.

claim: v0.9 adds router high availability: a multi-EPP topology where non-leader replicas keep their datastores populated and route traffic normally rather than returning 503, plus a --drain-timeout flag for graceful shutdown during rolling updates.
stance_target: the router's data-layer/discovery design already supports multi-replica operation, relevant when the discovery source is a custom non-k8s backend
quoted_support: Router high availability introduces a multi-EPP topology where non-leader replicas keep their datastores populated and route traffic rather than returning 503.

claim: v0.9 adds GPU-utilization-aware routing using a DCGM extractor and a 'generic endpoint-attribute filter and scorer' that routes on actual GPU utilization metrics instead of proxy signals like queue depth.
stance_target: the router already exposes a generalized, engine-agnostic attribute-based filter/scorer primitive that a custom backend could populate with its own metrics
quoted_support: GPU utilization-aware routing uses the DCGM extractor and a generic endpoint-attribute filter and scorer to route requests based on actual GPU utilization metrics rather than proxy signals like queue depth.

claim: The v0.10 roadmap (targeting September 2026) names 'a standardized model server interface' as a priority: a common API to query engine capabilities, manage lifecycle, and configure runtime parameters, independent of whether the underlying engine is vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.
stance_target: llm-d project itself is moving toward an engine/backend-agnostic abstraction, which a non-k8s-pod backend customization effort could align with or build ahead of
scope_conditions: stated as roadmap intent for v0.10, not yet implemented as of v0.9 blog (2026)
quoted_support: A standardized model server interface. The control plane needs a common API to query engine capabilities, manage lifecycle, and configure runtime parameters - independent of whether the engine underneath is vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM.

claim: RL rollout integration (veRL, vime) and time-slicing (architecture proposal at llm-d/llm-d/proposals/rl-time-slicing-platform.md) are explicitly labeled incubation-stage as of v0.9, with APIs still evolving; full RL story targets v0.10 and beyond, and time-slicing targets the 45-66% of accelerator time synchronous RL loops typically leave idle.
stance_target: maturity level of RL-related non-Kubernetes integration work, relevant caveat for anyone building on it
scope_conditions: llm-d v0.9 release, 2026; RL work in llm-d-incubation/llm-d-rl and llm-d-incubation/llm-d-rl-time-slicing repos
quoted_support: This work is incubation-stage - APIs are evolving and production hardening is ahead. The full RL story targets v0.10 and beyond.

claim: v0.9 renames EPP KV metrics to the llm_d_router_epp subsystem, with deprecated aliases available during a transition period, requiring dashboard/alert updates.
stance_target: metric-naming detail relevant to anyone building observability atop a customized router
quoted_support: The metric renames in this release (EPP KV metrics move to the `llm_d_router_epp` subsystem) require dashboard and alert updates - deprecated aliases are available during the transition.
